draft.title: Water's unusual properties
card: A water molecule is polar. The hydrogen atoms of one molecule are attracted to the oxygen atom of a neighbour. This attraction is a hydrogen bond, and it is stronger than the weak forces between most small molecules.

Compare the hydrides of Group 16: H2S, H2Se and H2Te. Their boiling points rise as the molecules get larger. Water breaks this pattern and boils at a much higher temperature than all of them, because extra energy is needed to overcome its hydrogen bonds.
In liquid water, hydrogen bonds keep forming and breaking as the molecules move past each other and sit close together.

In ice, each molecule is held by hydrogen bonds in a fixed, open lattice with gaps in it. This spaces the molecules further apart than in the liquid, so ice is less dense than liquid water and floats.
draft.remember: Hydrogen bonding lifts water's boiling point and gives ice an open structure, so ice floats.

a.q: Why does water boil at a higher temperature than H2S, even though H2S has more electrons?
opts: Hydrogen bonds between water molecules take more energy to break
Water molecules are larger than H2S molecules
The O-H bonds inside water molecules are easier to break
Water molecules have no attraction to each other when liquid
a.why: Boiling separates whole molecules, so it must overcome the attractions between them. Water's hydrogen bonds are stronger than the forces between H2S molecules, so more energy is needed. Size does not explain it, because water is the smallest of these molecules.
a.clue: Boiling pulls molecules apart from each other, not atoms apart within a molecule.

b.q: A lake in Victoria's high country freezes in winter. Which statement best explains why the ice forms a layer on top of the water?
opts: Hydrogen bonds hold ice in an open lattice, so it is less dense
Ice molecules are lighter than liquid water molecules
Hydrogen bonds break as water freezes, so ice is less dense
Cold water molecules move faster and rise to the surface
b.why: In ice, hydrogen bonds hold the molecules in a fixed open lattice with gaps, so the molecules are further apart and the ice is less dense. The molecules themselves are the same in both states, so ice is not made of lighter molecules. Hydrogen bonds do not break on freezing, they hold molecules in place.
b.clue: The molecules are identical in ice and water, so think about how they are arranged.
